Import mode (base tables)
A copy of the data is stored in the model. Fast and flexible for DAX, but it only changes when you press Refresh.
DirectQuery (Q1 to Q5)
Each visual sends the native SQL to PostgreSQL live. Always current, and ideal for proving SQL = DAX.
Power BI PMO course · 3
Lecture 1 · Connect
Connect Power BI to the SQL database, not to CSV files
Steps in Power BI Desktop
  1. Home › Get data › PostgreSQL database
  2. Server: localhost · Database: MahamDB
  3. Mode Import: tick the pmo_* and sys_* tables
  4. For each report query: Get data again, choose DirectQuery, open Advanced options and paste the SQL statement
  5. Name the query (Q1 … Q5) and give it a description
What Power Query writes (M)
let   Source = Value.NativeQuery(     PostgreSQL.Database(       "localhost", "MahamDB"),     "SELECT ... FROM pmo_task ...",     null, [EnableFolding = true]) in   Source
EnableFolding lets Power BI wrap your SQL with its own filters, so slicers still reach the database.
Power BI PMO course · 4
Lecture 1 · Project format
Save as a Power BI Project (.pbip)
File › Save as › Power BI project files. The report becomes readable text files that you can version in Git, compare and edit with scripts.
DAX Measures (PMO Portal).pbip ├─ *.SemanticModel/definition/ │  ├─ model.tmdl, relationships.tmdl │  ├─ tables/_Measures.tmdl … │  └─ cultures/en-US.tmdl, ar-SA.tmdl └─ *.Report/definition/    ├─ pages/pages.json    └─ pages/<id>/visuals/<id>/visual.json
TMDL = the model
Tables, columns, measures, relationships and translations as text.
PBIR = the report
One folder per page, one visual.json per visual.
Golden rule
Close Power BI Desktop before editing files, and keep only one window of the project open.

Power BI PMO course · 7
Lecture 2 · Dates
One Calendar for periods, one Snapshot for “as at”
Calendar (calculated table, marked as date table)
Calendar = ADDCOLUMNS (  CALENDAR (DATE(2025,1,1), DATE(2027,12,31)),  "Year", YEAR ([Date]),  "Month", FORMAT ([Date], "YYYY-MM"),  "MonthName", FORMAT ([Date], "MMM yyyy"),  "Quarter", "Q" & FORMAT ([Date], "Q"))
Snapshot (disconnected parameter)
Snapshot Date =  SELECTEDVALUE ('Snapshot'[Snapshot],   DATE (2026, 9, 30))
  • Sort MonthName by Month (YYYY-MM)
  • Turn off Auto date/time: it created 40 hidden LocalDateTables
  • Snapshot has no relationship: measures read it
Power BI PMO course · 8
Lecture 3 · SQL query 1
Overdue incomplete tasks
SELECT t.task_id, t.title AS task_title,        p.code AS project_code, p.name AS project_name,        COALESCE(u.nickname, u.username,             '(unassigned)') AS assignee,        t.status, t.priority, t.due_date,        DATE '2026-09-30' - t.due_date AS days_overdue FROM   pmo_task t JOIN   pmo_project p ON p.project_id = t.project_id LEFT JOIN sys_user u ON u.userid = t.assignee_user_id WHERE  t.due_date < DATE '2026-09-30'   AND  t.status <> 'Done' ORDER BY days_overdue DESC, p.name;
Business rule
Due strictly before the snapshot and status is not Done.
Why each join
INNER to project (every task has one). LEFT to user, so unassigned tasks still appear.
Result at 30 Sep 2026
22 to 23 rows, depending on the last data load.
Power BI PMO course · 9
Lecture 3 · SQL query 2
Project financial performance
WITH budget AS (  SELECT p.project_id, p.initial_approved_budget   + COALESCE(SUM(r.amount) FILTER    (WHERE r.status = 'Approved'), 0) AS approved_budget  FROM pmo_project p LEFT JOIN pmo_budget_revision r   ON r.project_id = p.project_id GROUP BY p.project_id), spend AS (  SELECT project_id, SUM(amount) FILTER (WHERE status =   'Posted' AND txn_date <= DATE '2026-09-30') AS actual_spend  FROM pmo_cost_transaction GROUP BY project_id), ftc AS (  SELECT project_id, SUM(forecast_amount) FILTER   (WHERE kind = 'ForecastToComplete') AS ftc  FROM pmo_financial_forecast GROUP BY project_id) SELECT b.*, s.actual_spend, s.actual_spend + f.ftc AS eac … FROM budget b LEFT JOIN spend s … LEFT JOIN ftc f …
Avoid fan-out
Joining budget, cost and forecast rows in one flat join multiplies amounts. Aggregate each fact per project first, then join one row to one row.
Definitions
Approved = initial + approved revisions Actual = posted, on or before snapshot Utilization = actual ÷ approved EAC = actual + forecast to complete Variance = approved − EAC
Power BI PMO course · 10 · abridged, full query in the tutorial document
Lecture 3 · SQL queries 3 and 4
High-exposure risks and period spend
Q3 · Open risks with score ≥ 12
SELECT r.risk_id, r.title, r.kind,   p.name AS project_name,   r.probability, r.impact,   r.score AS exposure_score, r.status FROM pmo_risk r JOIN pmo_project p USING (project_id) WHERE r.status = 'Open'   AND r.score >= 12 ORDER BY r.score DESC;
Score = probability × impact. Closed and Mitigating risks never count as open.
Q4 · Monthly actual and forecast
SELECT to_char(date_trunc('month', txn_date),   'YYYY-MM') AS period_month, project_id,   'Actual' AS series, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM pmo_cost_transaction WHERE status = 'Posted'   AND txn_date <= DATE '2026-09-30' GROUP BY 1, 2 UNION ALL SELECT …, 'Forecast', SUM(forecast_amount) FROM pmo_financial_forecast WHERE kind = 'ForecastToComplete' GROUP BY 1, 2;
One tidy table: a series column feeds a chart legend.
Power BI PMO course · 11
Lecture 3 · SQL query 5
Milestone status, and one snapshot everywhere
SELECT m.milestone_id, m.name AS milestone_name,   p.name AS project_name, m.due_date, m.status,   CASE    WHEN m.status = 'Achieved' THEN 'Achieved'    WHEN m.due_date < DATE '2026-09-30'     THEN 'Overdue'    ELSE 'Upcoming'   END AS roadmap_bucket FROM pmo_milestone m JOIN pmo_project p USING (project_id) ORDER BY m.due_date;
CASE turns raw statuses (Achieved, Missed, Pending) into a roadmap bucket relative to the snapshot.
Rule: one snapshot date
Every query uses DATE '2026-09-30'. The DAX Snapshot slicer defaults to the same day. Same date, same filters, so numbers can match.
Production tip
Replace the literal with a Power Query parameter, or with CURRENT_DATE, when the report goes live.

3 · Why explicit measures
  • One definition used by every visual
  • Business rules (status, snapshot) live in code, not in visual filters

  • A description on each measure documents the rule

Power BI PMO course · 13
Lecture 4 · Core measures
The five required measures
Overdue Tasks = VAR _snap = [Snapshot Date] RETURN CALCULATE (  COUNTROWS ('public pmo_task'),  'public pmo_task'[status] <> "Done",  'public pmo_task'[due_date] < _snap) + 0 Task Completion % = DIVIDE (  SUMX ('public pmo_task',   [weight] * [progress_pct]),  SUM ('public pmo_task'[weight])) / 100
Approved Budget = SUM ('public pmo_project'[initial_approved_budget]) + CALCULATE (SUM ('public pmo_budget_revision'[amount]),   'public pmo_budget_revision'[status] = "Approved") Actual Spend = VAR _snap = [Snapshot Date] RETURN CALCULATE (  SUM ('public pmo_cost_transaction'[amount]),  'public pmo_cost_transaction'[status] = "Posted",  'public pmo_cost_transaction'[txn_date] <= _snap) Budget Utilization % = DIVIDE ([Actual Spend], [Approved Budget])
Power BI PMO course · 14 · each measure mirrors the matching SQL rule
Lecture 4 · Forecast measures
Building on measures: EAC and variance
Forecast To Complete = CALCULATE (  SUM ('public pmo_financial_forecast'[forecast_amount]),  'public pmo_financial_forecast'[kind]   = "ForecastToComplete") EAC = [Actual Spend] + [Forecast To Complete] Projected Variance = [Approved Budget] - [EAC] Projected Overruns = COUNTROWS (FILTER (  VALUES ('public pmo_project'[project_id]),  [Projected Variance] < 0)) + 0
Watch the forecast kind
The table holds ForecastToComplete and MonthlyEstimate with the same total. Summing both doubles the forecast.
Business-readable formats
"AED "#,0 "AED "#,0;"AED "-#,0 0.0%
With display units = Millions a card shows AED 16.11M.

Lecture 5 · Visual settings
Settings that make it management-ready
Slicers
  • Dropdown style saves space
  • Snapshot: single select
  • Language: single select, default English
  • Sync slicers across pages
Cards
  • Display units: Millions, 2 decimals
  • Category label off; title carries the name
  • Same size, one row of six
  • Rounded border, no shadow
Charts and table
  • Month axis sorted by Month key
  • Title states the unit (AED)
  • Subtitle off when it repeats the title
  • Scorecard with totals row
Colour rule
Navy for structure, blue for actuals, dark blue for forecast or EAC. Every status is also written in words, never colour alone.

Lecture 6 · Explaining discrepancies
When numbers differ, a rule differs
KPI
Typical cause found in this data
Effect at 30 Sep 2026
Overdue tasks
“Due on or before” instead of “strictly before”
+1 task due exactly on 30 Sep
Overdue tasks
Import refreshed earlier than DirectQuery reads live
23 vs 22 until you press Refresh
Open high risks
Counting Mitigating, or ignoring status
6 → 13 → 15
Actual spend
Including drafts or transactions after the snapshot
+AED 429,958 drafts, +AED 75,000 later
Approved budget
Revision approved after the snapshot date
AED 1,500 (as-at measure shows it)
Forecast / EAC
Summing every forecast kind
Forecast doubles (two equal kinds)
Task completion
Weighted, simple average, or Done count
62.5% vs 59.3% vs 26.2%

Lecture 7 · Steps 1 and 2
Language table, Lang measure, label measures
-- 1. New table Language = DATATABLE (  "LangCode", STRING, "Language", STRING,  "LangSort", INTEGER,  { { "en", "English", 1 }, { "ar", "العربية", 2 } }) -- 2. Current language (English by default) Lang = SELECTEDVALUE ('Language'[LangCode], "en") -- 3. One label measure per text on the page Lbl Approved Budget = IF ([Lang] = "ar", "الميزانية المعتمدة",     "Approved budget")
  • Sort Language by LangSort; hide LangSort
  • Put labels in a display folder: 6 Language
  • About 40 labels: headers, slicer and card titles, chart titles, notes
  • Snapshot Label also switches its date format
Power BI PMO course · 22
Lecture 7 · Step 3
Translate data values with calculated columns
-- in 'public pmo_task' status_ar = SWITCH ([status],  "Done", "منجزة", "InProgress", "قيد التنفيذ",  "ToDo", "لم تبدأ", "Blocked", "متوقفة",  [status]) -- in 'public pmo_project' status_ar = SWITCH ([status],  "Active", "نشط", "OnHold", "معلّق",  "Planning", "تخطيط", "Completed", "مكتمل",  [status]) -- in Calendar (Sort by column: Month) MonthNameAr = SWITCH (MONTH ([Date]),  1, "يناير", 2, "فبراير", … 12, "ديسمبر")  & " " & YEAR ([Date])
Why SWITCH, not FORMAT
FORMAT with "ar-SA" uses the Hijri calendar. An explicit list keeps Gregorian month names.
The last argument
Returning [status] for unknown values means a new status still shows, untranslated, instead of blank.
Keep proper nouns
Project names stay as stored in the database.

FP Scorecard: 9 English rows + 9 Arabic rows, each pointing to the same column or measure.

  3. Add a fourth value: "en" or "ar"
  4. Relate [FP … Lang] (many) to Language[LangCode] (one), single direction
  5. Use the parameter in the visual instead of the fields
("Actual spend", NAMEOF(  '_Measures'[Actual Spend]), 0, "en"), ("الإنفاق الفعلي", NAMEOF(  '_Measures'[Actual Spend]), 2, "ar")

Lecture 7 · Step 5
Bind every visible text to a measure
Visual titles
Format › General › Title › Text › fx › Format style: Field value › choose Lbl … measure.
Cards: turn the category label off and use the title.
Page headers
Text boxes cannot switch. Use a card whose value is the header measure, navy background, white 18 pt text.
Language slicer
Field: Language[Language]. Single select, English selected, then View › Sync slicers on every page.
// what a measure-bound title looks like inside visual.json (PBIR) "title": [{ "properties": { "text": { "expr": { "Measure": {   "Expression": { "SourceRef": { "Entity": "_Measures" } },   "Property": "Lbl Chart Spend" } } } } }]
Power BI PMO course · 25
Lecture 7 · Step 6
Model translations for Power BI Service
Add the ar-SA culture and translate captions of tables, columns and measures. Saved as cultures/ar-SA.tmdl:
cultureInfo ar-SA  translations   model Model    table 'public pmo_project'     caption: المشاريع     column name      caption: اسم المشروع    table _Measures     measure 'Approved Budget'      caption: الميزانية المعتمدة
How to add them
Tabular Editor, the Translations Builder, or edit the TMDL file with Desktop closed. This project has 91 captions.
Where it shows
Power BI Service, for users whose browser language is Arabic: field list and default visual names. Desktop does not show them.

Power BI PMO course · 27
Lecture 8 · Lessons learned
Problems we hit, and the fix
Symptom
Cause and fix
Changes disappeared after reopening
A second Desktop window saved over the files. Keep one window open.
“Can’t determine relationships between the fields”
Hand-written visual.json lacked the field-parameter expansion.
DAX and SQL differ by a little
Imported tables older than DirectQuery: Refresh, then compare.
“needs to be recalculated”
New calculated objects: run a Calculate refresh.
Cards show 16.11MAED
Currency as a suffix: use a prefix, "AED "#,0.
Arabic months in Hijri
FORMAT with ar-SA: use an explicit SWITCH list.
Power BI PMO course · 28
Lecture 8 · Practise
Exercises to implement on your own
1 · Milestone measures
Add a milestone roadmap visual using Overdue Milestones and Milestones Achieved %, with Arabic titles.
2 · Use the inactive date
Write Tasks Due by Month with USERELATIONSHIP on task[due_date] → Calendar[Date].
3 · Parameterise the snapshot
Replace DATE '2026-09-30' in Q1 to Q5 with a Power Query parameter and check SQL still equals DAX.
4 · Add the web as a third source
Add the web dashboard as a third card in each reconciliation pair and document every gap.
5 · Translate a new visual
Add a risks-by-project chart: label measure, field parameter for the legend, risk kind in Arabic.
Done when
Each language shows no leftover text from the other, and every KPI reconciles.
